reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that individual variation in mental imagery modality (visual, auditory, etc.) directly impacts how brain lesions manifest as symptoms. This creates a dual structure: a modality-dependent neural architecture and a lesion-dependent symptom expression. The mathematical framework treats modality M(I) as a latent variable influencing the mapping from lesion L to symptom S. When lesion L occurs, its effect on symptom S depends on whether it disrupts a frequently used neural tract (high T) or a less-used one (low T), where resilience R(T,L) determines outcome. The Charcot case exemplifies this: a highly visual thinker's lesion affecting visual memory pathways leads to profound amnesia, whereas a similar lesion in a non-visual thinker might be asymptomatic due to compensatory mechanisms. This duality implies a probabilistic model where P(S|L,M) = P(S|L) × P(M|L), enabling Bayesian prediction of symptom profiles given lesion data and known modality.
